name: Creative Thinking Performance Test (CTPT)
description: Background The assessment of creative thinking in science faces challenges in measuring creative abilities through student performance, particularly when students need to represent multidimensional constructs through contextual tasks. The study aims to develop and validate the Creative Thinking Performance Test (CTPT) to measure creative thinking performance in a science context across four dimensions: sensitivity, flexibility, novelty, and elaboration. Methods The CTPT was developed through content validation by experts and item refinement, then analyzed using the Rasch model to evaluate item functions, fit, reliability, separation, and Rasch model parameters. The evaluation of item characteristics and the coverage of participants’ abilities utilized the Item Characteristic Curve (ICC), Category Probability Curve (CPC), and person–item histogram/map. Evidence of external validity was obtained through independent science-based problem-solving performance. Results The overall Aiken’s V for the items ranged from .93 to .96, and all items were retained. The MNSQ infit values ranged from .81 to 1.48, and the MNSQ outfit values ranged from .81 to 1.49, with Pt-Measure correlations ranging from.55 to.74. Item reliability reached.94 and person reliability.80, while person separation was 2.02.
